root_cause: The datepicker popup element is focusable and intercepts the Tab key, trapping focus inside the datepicker and preventing focus from moving to the next form field.
repair_strategy: Make the datepicker element non-focusable by setting tabindex="-1", allowing the Tab key to bypass the popup and move focus to the next focusable element.
expected_accessibility_effect: When the datepicker is open, pressing Tab will move focus from the visit date input to the next form field (the access notes input), allowing keyboard-only users to continue filling the form without being trapped.
functional_risks: None significant; datepicker remains operable via arrow keys, Enter, and mouse interactions.
Setting tabindex=-1 removes the popup from the tab order, which is appropriate for a modal-like dialog and does not affect screen reader perception of the datepicker's content.
verification_requirements: Pressing Tab while the datepicker is open moves focus to the #notes input.
Arrow keys still navigate dates within the datepicker.
Enter key still selects the focused date and closes the datepicker.
Datepicker still opens on focus or click of the visit date input.
Datepicker still hides appropriately when a date is selected or when clicking outside.
